hints: Look closely at Y first and name it, counting its carbons to see what size starting material you need.
Remember that acid hydrolysis of a nitrile keeps the same carbon skeleton, so only a 3-carbon nitrile can give a 3-carbon acid.
For the esters, think about which part becomes the acid on hydrolysis, the acyl part before the O, and match it to Y.
walkthrough:
**Identify Y**

Great start, let's see what we are trying to make. Y has $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2$ joined to $\text{C(=O)OH}$.

That is propanoic acid:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$

**Check the nitriles by hydrolysis**

Nitriles hydrolyse in one step with dilute acid to give a carboxylic acid with the same number of carbons.

$$\text{R-C}{\equiv}\text{N} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+, \text{heat}} \text{R-COOH} + \text{NH}_3$$

**Apply to 1 and 2**

1. propanenitrile is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$. Hydrolysis gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, which is Y. So 1 works.

2. ethanenitrile is $\text{CH}_3\text{CN}$. Hydrolysis gives $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ (ethanoic acid), one carbon too short. So 2 does not work.

**Check the esters by hydrolysis**

Esters hydrolyse in one step with dilute acid to give a carboxylic acid from the acyl part plus an alcohol from the alkyl part.

$$\text{R-COO-R'} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+, \text{heat}} \text{R-COOH} + \text{R'OH}$$

**Apply to 3 and 4**

3. propyl ethanoate is $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. The acid part is ethanoate, so you get ethanoic acid, not Y. So 3 does not work.

4. ethyl propanoate is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. The acid part is propanoate, so you get propanoic acid, which is Y. So 4 works.

Together, 1 and 4 make Y in a single step.

options.A: 1 is correct because propanenitrile hydrolyses to propanoic acid, but 3 is wrong because propyl ethanoate hydrolyses to ethanoic acid plus propan-1-ol. The propyl group becomes the alcohol, not the acid.
options.B: Both work. 1, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$, gives propanoic acid on acid hydrolysis. 4, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOC}_2\text{H}_5$, gives propanoic acid plus ethanol on acid hydrolysis. Both are single-step routes to Y.
options.C: Both are wrong for Y. 2, ethanenitrile, gives ethanoic acid (2 carbons, not 3). 3, propyl ethanoate, also gives ethanoic acid. This choice confuses the alcohol part of the ester with the acid part.
options.D: 4 is correct because ethyl propanoate gives propanoic acid, but 2 is wrong because ethanenitrile gives ethanoic acid. A nitrile cannot gain an extra carbon on hydrolysis, so a 2-carbon nitrile can never make a 3-carbon acid.
